land.text: Aden and the Lahij oasis, ruled by the Banu Ma'n until the brothers were placed in power in 1083

predecessors.note: The Zurayids were Sulayhid governors and tributaries until about 1110. The Ma'nids of Aden (defeated by Ali al-Sulayhi in 1062) have no dossier.

land.text: Aden and the Zurayid lands, conquered 22 June 1174 by Turan Shah

successors.note: Cliopatria's Ayyubid Sultanate row starts in 1177; its Nabhani and Mahdid rows (1169-1176) are not the Zurayid successors.

capitals.name: Aden
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Centre of power: Aden'; the inland branch worked from at-Ta'kar and later Dhu Jibla.

rulers.note: Inland line (Ta'kar). The coastal line ran in parallel: al-Mas'ud bin al-Karam 1083-1110, Abi al-Gharat from 1110, to Ali bin Muhammad bin Abi al-Gharat, killed 1150.

rulers.note: The page gives no transfer year between the two (Saba's end is 1138).

correction.text: Aden and the Lahij oasis, the Zurayid coast (3,310 km2): the shape unchanged, years 1083-1147

keyframe_review.note: 3,310 km2 for 1085-1168: Aden and Lahij (4 and 7 cells). Page: the brothers 'were placed in power in 1083' (Cliopatria starts two years late; the page's dynasty dates are 1083-1174); al-Msaod handled shipping from al-Khadra and al-Abbas inland trade from Ta'kar (not in the shape); the coastal line of al-Msaod was pushed out of Aden in 1138 and 'killed in the battle of Za'za' in Lahij in 1150', so Lahij stays inside the one dynasty throughout. The shape is right for the coastal state to 1147; from 1148 the highlands are added (new keyframe zurayid-dynasty_1148). The page gives no area. Review fix: keyframes 1 and 2 and the 1083 found event now use this same Aden-and-Lahij shape (the first draft used the whole Aden and Lahij governorates, about 21,000 km2 with Ibb, from 1139).

correction.text: Aden and the Lahij oasis (the 1085 shape) with the Ibb highlands: Dhu Jibla, at-Ta'kar, Ibb and Habb, years 1148-1168

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1148-1168. Page: 'A decade later [than the open warfare of 1138] the ruler Muhammad bin Saba bought a number of important Sulayhid fortresses and towns' (Dhu Jibla, al-Takar, Ibb, Habb), so c. 1148 at confidence 1 (the page gives no year; Muhammad bin Saba reigned 1139-1153); and 'Zurayid influence in the highlands lasted until about 1193'. The towns lie inside the Ibb governorate; their extent is my reading. The page also says 'After the defeat of Al-Msaod branch, The Zurayid sphere of power stretched from Taiz to Dhofar' (after 1150), which names no towns or years and is not drawn. Review fix: Aden and Lahij are now the 1085 shape, as in keyframe 0 (the first draft used the whole governorates).

correction.text: Aden and the Lahij oasis (the 1169 shape, the same two cells as 1085) with the Ibb highlands until the Ayyubid conquest of Aden on 22 June 1174; years 1169-1174

keyframe_review.note: 3,310 km2 for 1169-1176, the same two cells as 1085. Page: 'When the Ayyubids conquered Aden on 22 June 1174 the rule of the Zurayids ended', so 1175 and 1176 are two years too many; the Mahdids of Zabid 'besieged Aden in 1164' and were beaten in 1173 with the Hamdanid sultan of Sana'a's help. The highland towns are in the 1148 keyframe. The Ayyubid conquest of the highlands (Turan-Shah, 1173-1174) is on a page not opened.

ledger.note: 1083: the brothers al-Abbas and al-Mas'ud are set over Aden. Page: 'The brothers were placed in power in 1083 and shared the governmental affairs between them'; dynasty 1083-1174. The Sulayhid page: 'In Aden the Zurayids... came to power in 1083, at first as Sulayhid tributaries'; independent 'After 1110'. Review fix: the region is the 1085 Cliopatria shape (Aden and the Lahij oasis), as in keyframe 0.

region.text: Dhu Jibla, al-Takar, Ibb and Habb

ledger.counterpart: Sulayhid remnant (holders of the highland fortresses)
ledger.note: c. 1148: the inland line of Muhammad bin Saba buys the highland fortresses and towns round Ibb. Page: 'The two lines met in open warfare in 1138' and 'A decade later the ruler Muhammad bin Saba bought a number of important Sulayhid fortresses and towns' (Dhu Jibla, al-Takar, Ibb, Habb), after marrying the last Sulayhid queen; no year is given, so 1148 is the page's 'a decade later' (Muhammad bin Saba reigned 1139-1153, Arwa died 1138). The Sulayhid dossier ends in 1138, so there is no mirror loss; the counterpart is the Sulayhid remnant that sold the fortresses.

region.text: Aden, the Lahij oasis and the Ibb highlands

ledger.note: 1174: the Ayyubids take Aden and end the Zurayids. Page: 'When the Ayyubids conquered Aden on 22 June 1174 the rule of the Zurayids ended'; Yasir bin Bilal was handed over to Turan Shah, who executed him in 1175; Zurayid influence in the highlands lasted until about 1193. Cliopatria keeps the Zurayids to 1176. Review fix: region is the 1169 shape plus Ibb, as in keyframe 2.

wars.name: Siege of Zabid (1110)
wars.outcome: The Zurayid brothers joined the Sulayhid al-Mufaddal's campaign against Zabid and were both killed in the siege; the Zurayids ruled Aden independently for more than sixty years afterwards.

wars.name: Zurayid civil war
wars.outcome: 'The two lines met in open warfare in 1138' and the coastal line of al-Msaod was pushed out of Aden; Ali bin Abi al-Gharat of that line 'was killed in the battle of Za'za' in Lahij in 1150' and the inland line of al-Abbas ruled alone. Both lines are inside this one dossier, so there is no merge event.

wars.name: Mahdid siege of Aden
wars.outcome: The Mahdids of Zabid besieged Aden in 1164; with the Hamdanid sultan of Sana'a's help the Zurayids 'utterly defeat the Mahdid ruler Abd an-Nabi in 1173'.

wars.name: Ayyubid conquest of Aden
wars.outcome: The Ayyubids conquered Aden on 22 June 1174, ending the Zurayids.

certainty.note: Aden is a city-port and Lahij a named plain; the highland holdings after c. 1148 are towns, not areas.

notes:
Pages: the Zurayids page (infobox blank except for dynasty dates) and the Sulayhid page (budget 1-2). The Zurayids page names no area, so the Cliopatria shape (Aden and Lahij, 3,310 km2) stands for the coast; the highlands from c. 1148 ('a decade later' than the 1138 war) are a new keyframe and an undated gain (confidence 1).
Cliopatria starts the Zurayids in 1085 (page: 1083) and ends them in 1176 (page: 22 June 1174); its neighbour list shows the Nabhani row 1169-1176, which is an Omani artefact and not a successor.
The Zurayids were Sulayhid tributaries from 1083 to about 1110 (Sulayhid page: 'at first as Sulayhid tributaries'; Zurayids page: independent 'After 1110'); the Sulayhid dossier records the vassal_start 1083 and vassal_end 1110.
Counterparts without a dossier: the Ma'nids of Aden, hamdanids-of-sanaa (the sultan of Sana'a who helped in 1173), mahdids (the Mahdids of Zabid, 1158-1174; Cliopatria's Mahdids row is in Oman). ayyubid-sultanate exists in polities.csv from 1177 only.
Not opened: the Ayyubid conquest of Yemen page (Turan-Shah, 1173-1174), which would give the highland campaign.
Review repair (2026-10-20): (1) Aden and Lahij are one shape throughout (the 1085 Cliopatria cells, 3,310 km2); the first draft's whole-governorate union is gone from the found event, keyframes 1-2, the dissolve event and identity. (2) The highland purchase moved from 1139 to c. 1148 (page: 'A decade later' than 1138). (3) The 1150 'merge' with the coastal line is deleted: both Zurayid lines are inside this dossier; the end of the civil war is told in the war record (coastal line expelled from Aden in 1138, Ali bin Abi al-Gharat killed at Za'za' in Lahij in 1150). (4) Not carried, page silent on towns and years: 'After the defeat of Al-Msaod branch, The Zurayid sphere of power stretched from Taiz to Dhofar', and the Ayyubid conquest of the highlands (Turan-Shah page, not opened).
